Topic 10 · Lab 2

From bronze to gold

Wednesday at Ventolia Energy. The daily report works, and now management wants to know how the turbines really behave, from the SCADA readings every 10 minutes. Those readings arrive raw and with errors. You will read the code of a classic medallion pipeline (bronze, silver, gold) and orchestrate it with a job that runs three loads in parallel.

1Read the bronze notebook8 min

What you are looking atBronze is the faithful copy of what arrived: no cleaning and nothing thrown away. It only adds metadata about the load, so that every row says when it was loaded, from which file and by which job run.
  1. You should seeTwo text boxes at the top of the notebook, source and run_id: the widgets the cell creates.
    2. Python
    # Values sent by the job task. The defaults let you run the notebook by hand.
dbutils.widgets.text("source", "scada")      # turbines, scada or work_orders
dbutils.widgets.text("run_id", "manual")     # the job sends {{job.run_id}}

SOURCE = dbutils.widgets.get("source")
RUN_ID = dbutils.widgets.get("run_id")
CATALOG = "lab1002"

print(f"Loading source '{SOURCE}' (run {RUN_ID})")

    The job will run this same notebook three times, each with a different source. run_id will receive the run identifier, so you can trace every row back to the run that loaded it.

    3. Python
    from pyspark.sql import functions as F

raw = (spark.read
       .option("header", "true")
       .csv(f"/Volumes/{CATALOG}/landing/data/{SOURCE}*.csv"))

print(f"{raw.count()} rows read")
raw.printSchema()
    Python
    bronze = (raw
          .withColumn("_ingested_at", F.current_timestamp())
          .withColumn("_source_file", F.col("_metadata.file_name"))
          .withColumn("_job_run_id", F.lit(RUN_ID)))

    No inferSchema: every column stays as text, exactly as in the file. _metadata.file_name is a hidden column Spark offers on any file it reads.

    4. Python
    table = f"{CATALOG}.bronze.{SOURCE}"

(bronze.write
       .mode("overwrite")
       .option("overwriteSchema", "true")
       .saveAsTable(table))

print(f"{spark.table(table).count()} rows in {table}")
display(spark.table(table).limit(5))
  4. You should see5206 rows read, a schema where every column is string, and a table with three extra columns: _ingested_at, _source_file = scada_2026-10-21.csv and _job_run_id = manual.
    5. Check your understandingBronze keeps 5,206 readings even though some are clearly wrong. Why is it useful to keep them instead of cleaning them here?

2Read the silver notebook10 min

What you are looking atSilver is data you can trust: real types, quality rules applied and the bad rows removed. Do not run this notebook by hand: it needs the three bronze tables, and the job will create them.
    2. Python
    turbines = (spark.table(f"{CATALOG}.bronze.turbines")
            .select("turbine_id", "park_id", "park", "model",
                    F.col("rated_power_mw").cast("double").alias("rated_power_mw")))

work_orders = (spark.table(f"{CATALOG}.bronze.work_orders")
               .select("work_order_id", "turbine_id", "reason",
                       F.to_timestamp("start_time").alias("start_time"),
                       F.to_timestamp("end_time").alias("end_time")))

turbines.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable(f"{CATALOG}.silver.turbines")
work_orders.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable(f"{CATALOG}.silver.work_orders")
print(turbines.count(), "turbines |", work_orders.count(), "work orders")
    3. Python
    scada = (spark.table(f"{CATALOG}.bronze.scada")
         .select(F.to_timestamp("reading_time").alias("reading_time"),
                 "turbine_id",
                 F.col("wind_speed_ms").cast("double").alias("wind_speed_ms"),
                 F.col("power_kw").cast("double").alias("power_kw"),
                 "status", "_ingested_at", "_job_run_id"))

rows_in = scada.count()
print(rows_in, "readings from bronze")
    4. Python
    r1 = scada.dropDuplicates(["turbine_id", "reading_time"])
r2 = r1.filter(F.col("wind_speed_ms").isNotNull() & F.col("power_kw").isNotNull())
r3 = r2.filter(F.col("wind_speed_ms").between(0, 40))
r4 = r3.join(turbines.select("turbine_id", "rated_power_mw"), "turbine_id")
r5 = r4.filter(F.col("power_kw").between(0, F.col("rated_power_mw") * 1000 * 1.05))

clean = r5.drop("rated_power_mw")
    RuleWhat it removes in today's data
    1 · dropDuplicatesReadings sent twice by the SCADA export
    2 · isNotNullReadings without wind or power
    3 · between(0, 40)Wind of 80 m/s: a broken anemometer
    4 · join with the turbinesReadings from P04-WTG01, a turbine that is not in the master data
    5 · power ≤ 105 % of ratedReadings of 99,999 kW
    5. Python
    counts = [rows_in] + [df.count() for df in (r1, r2, r3, r4, r5)]
rules = ["1 · duplicates", "2 · empty values", "3 · impossible wind",
         "4 · unknown turbine", "5 · impossible power"]

report = spark.createDataFrame(
    [(rule, counts[i] - counts[i + 1]) for i, rule in enumerate(rules)]
    + [("rows kept", counts[-1])],
    ["rule", "rows"])
display(report)
    Check your understandingRule 4 is a join. What happens to the readings of a new turbine that has not been added to turbines.csv yet? Is that what the business wants? (Lab 1003 answers this with a quarantine table.)

3Read the gold SQL5 min

What you are looking atGold answers business questions. It only reads silver and groups it. It is plain SQL, and the job will run it on a SQL warehouse, not on the notebooks' serverless compute: each task chooses its own compute.
    2. SQL
    -- 1002 · 03 · Gold: the numbers the operations committee reads
--
-- Gold answers business questions. It reads only silver (clean, typed data)
-- and groups it. Each table is rebuilt in full on every run.

-- 1 · One row per wind farm and day
--     Readings arrive every 10 minutes, so each power value in kW lasts 1/6 h:
--     energy in MWh = sum(power_kw) / 6 / 1000.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab1002.gold.park_daily AS
SELECT
  t.park,
  CAST(s.reading_time AS DATE)                                     AS day,
  count(DISTINCT s.turbine_id)                                     AS turbines,
  round(sum(s.power_kw) / 6 / 1000, 1)                             AS energy_mwh,
  -- Share of readings in which the turbine was available (not in maintenance)
  round(100 * avg(CASE WHEN s.status = 'MAINTENANCE' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END), 1)
                                                                   AS availability_pct,
  -- Energy produced against the maximum the turbines could have produced
  round(100 * sum(s.power_kw) / 1000 / sum(t.rated_power_mw), 1)   AS capacity_factor_pct
FROM lab1002.silver.scada AS s
JOIN lab1002.silver.turbines AS t USING (turbine_id)
GROUP BY t.park, CAST(s.reading_time AS DATE);

-- 2 · One row per maintenance stop
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab1002.gold.maintenance_stops AS
SELECT
  w.work_order_id,
  t.park,
  w.turbine_id,
  w.reason,
  round((unix_timestamp(w.end_time) - unix_timestamp(w.start_time)) / 3600, 1) AS hours_stopped
FROM lab1002.silver.work_orders AS w
JOIN lab1002.silver.turbines AS t USING (turbine_id);

    Three formulas worth a second look: energy (each 10-minute reading in kW lasts 1/6 of an hour), availability (share of readings not in maintenance) and capacity factor (energy produced against what the turbines could have produced at full power).

6Break it and repair it7 min

What you are looking atA typo in a parameter breaks one load. Instead of running the whole job again, Repair run runs only the task that failed and the ones that depend on it.
  1. Why thisLook at Retries: Immediately, at most 3x. Notebook tasks on serverless are retried automatically, so the run will try bronze_orders again before giving up. A typo is not a temporary error: you will see the retries fail too.
  2. You should seeThe new run with a red cross. In the chart, bronze_orders red, bronze_scada and bronze_turbines green, and silver and gold pale: they never ran, because they depend on the failed task.
  3. Why thisThe notebook reads {source}*.csv, a pattern. A typo that still matches the file, such as work_order, would not break anything: the pattern would still find work_orders.csv.
    You should see[PATH_NOT_FOUND] Path does not exist: …/landing/data/work-orders*.csv, and at the top Retry: 1st (latest) · Failed: the automatic retry failed too.
  6. You should seebronze_orders failed, bronze_scada and bronze_turbines succeeded, silver and gold Upstream failed. The button says 3: only bronze_orders, silver and gold run again.
  7. You should seeThe same run, now green, with the two bronze loads that worked kept as they were. Run the gold queries of block 5 again: same figures.
    8. Check your understandingRepair run saved two bronze loads. In a real pipeline with fifty tasks and two hours of runtime, what does that mean?
End of the labYou have a medallion pipeline orchestrated by a job: three loads in parallel, a validation step that waits for all of them, and a gold layer on a SQL warehouse. When something breaks, you repair only what failed. In lab 1003 the pipeline starts by itself when a file arrives and decides what to do with the rows that cannot be fixed.
